title: Understanding and Mitigating Covert Channel and Side Channel Vulnerabilities Introduced by RowHammer Defenses
problem: Modern RowHammer defenses (PRAC, RFM) introduce timing covert and side channels because their preventive refresh actions block DRAM access in ways that depend on application memory access patterns, allowing adversaries to both observe victim access behavior and establish covert communication channels. No prior work has analyzed these defense-induced timing vulnerabilities.
motivation: Widely-deployed RowHammer mitigations in DDR5 (PRAC) and DDR4 (RFM) are assumed to be purely defensive, but their observable bandwidth-reduction side effects create a new attack surface that undermines the security guarantees of the defenses themselves.
method: The paper introduces LeakyHammer, a class of attacks exploiting the timing latency increase caused by RowHammer preventive refresh actions. Two covert channels are built: one exploiting PRAC's per-row activation counter responses and one exploiting RFM's refresh management commands, both causing measurable DRAM latency spikes observable by a spy process. A proof-of-concept website fingerprinting attack identifies visited websites by correlating RowHammer-preventive action patterns triggered by a victim's browsing. Three countermeasures (randomized refresh scheduling, access pattern obfuscation, and noise injection) are evaluated.
key_novelty: First systematic demonstration that RowHammer defense mechanisms themselves (PRAC and RFM) can be weaponized as covert and side channels via defense-induced DRAM bandwidth throttling.
contributions: First analysis of timing covert and side channel vulnerabilities introduced by state-of-the-art RowHammer defenses (PRAC and RFM)
LeakyHammer covert channel achieving 39.0 Kbps (PRAC) and 48.7 Kbps (RFM) channel capacity
Proof-of-concept website fingerprinting side channel exploiting RowHammer-preventive actions
Evaluation of three countermeasures showing that fundamentally eliminating LeakyHammer incurs large performance overhead in highly RowHammer-vulnerable systems
limitations: Proposed countermeasures incur large performance overheads, and the paper does not provide a practical zero-cost mitigation for LeakyHammer.
primary_theme: RowHammer defense-induced timing side and covert channels
